body: What is your application language and how did you configure the validator?
I can confirm the issue. I think it is caused by the intl parser stopping after it has parsed the pattern and does not check if there are remaining characters...

According to the documentation of IntlDateFormatter class:

> Converts string $value to an incremental time value, starting at $parse_pos 
> and consuming as much of the input value as possible. 

http://php.net/manual/en/intldateformatter.parse.php

Don't know if related but I also have problem with ICU date format. In rules() I have:

`
['lBirthDate', 'date', 'format' => 'dd/mm/yyyy'],
`
that wrongly accepts dates in format dd/mm/yyy without any error (as far I can see the validator just try to calculate the timestamp, if it succedeed then the it returns true)

while using
`
['lBirthDate', 'date', 'format' => 'php:d/m/Y'],
`
the validator works correctly

Tested on windows 7, 64bit, php 5.6.5, yii 61fc0f0
@massimilianomancini can you give some example input that produces the problem?
I mean a date value that you enter in the text field.
I tried with different dates in short italian format dd/mm/yy for example 07/10/74 or 12/07/69

issue.body:
DateValidator sets the time part to 00:00:00 when inserting the timestamp into timestampAttribute, because [here](https://github.com/yiisoft/yii2/blob/58becaceab5cf3f7896d7934de715cecfd95c210/framework/validators/DateValidator.php#L133) the `$timetype` argument is set to `IntlDateFormatter::None`.
It doesn't help if you use `Yii::$app->formatter->datetimeFormat` as a format, because both `Yii::$app->formatter->datetimeFormat` and `Yii::$app->formatter->dateFormat` are "medium", so DateValidator doesn't know if you want to keep the time or not.

The other problem is that even though it cuts off the time part, it still accepts input that contains a time part.
